questions.stem: The word 'AVERSION' derives from the Latin root VERS (to turn away). Which phrase best captures its meaning in standard English usage?

options.option_text: a deep-seated dislike or feeling of turning away from something
a gradual shifting of attention toward something unfamiliar
an unexpected change in one's daily plans or schedule
an enthusiastic attraction toward a new activity or interest

questions.explanation: A is correct: 'aversion' derives from Latin 'aversio' — 'a turning away from' — and means a strong, settled dislike or repugnance. D is the opposite (attraction, not repulsion). B conflates it with 'diversion' (redirecting attention). C describes 'deviation' or 'diversion,' not aversion.

questions.stem: The words INTROVERT and EXTROVERT are formed with the root VERT (to turn), meaning 'inward-turned' and 'outward-turned' respectively. Which statement correctly captures their psychological distinction?

options.option_text: Introverts are naturally shy and timid; extroverts are naturally bold
Introverts recharge in solitude; extroverts recharge through socialising
Introverts avoid people permanently; extroverts seek attention at all times
Introverts are intellectually superior; extroverts are more physically active

questions.explanation: B is correct: Jung's original distinction is about where psychic energy is directed — inward (solitude restores the introvert) versus outward (social contact energises the extrovert). A is the single most common error; shyness and introversion are not synonymous — a person can be outgoing yet introverted in energy terms. C and D introduce absolute or unsupported claims.

questions.stem: A news report states: 'The minister's office acknowledged an inadvertent leak of the budget documents.' Based on the etymology IN + AD + VERT + ENT, what does 'inadvertent' specifically convey here?

options.option_text: the leak was a deliberate act disguised as an accident by officials
the leak involved classified data passed covertly to foreign parties
the leak resulted from inattention or failure to notice proper protocols
the leak was caused by a technical fault in the ministry's server system

questions.explanation: C is correct: 'inadvertent' literally means 'not turning (one's) attention toward' — implying an oversight or lapse of attention, not deliberate wrongdoing. A directly contradicts this (deliberate ≠ inadvertent). B confuses 'inadvertent' with 'covert.' D attributes the leak to a technical cause, which is a factual claim unrelated to the word's meaning.

questions.stem: In anatomy, 'TRANSVERSE' (Latin TRANS = across + VERSUS = turned) names one of three standard body planes. Which option correctly identifies the transverse plane?

options.option_text: a vertical plane that divides the body into front and back halves
a vertical plane that divides the body into left and right halves
a horizontal plane that divides the body into upper and lower halves
a diagonal plane that cuts through the body at a 45-degree angle

questions.explanation: C is correct: the transverse (axial/horizontal) plane 'turns across' the body, separating the superior portion from the inferior. A describes the coronal (frontal) plane; B describes the sagittal (median) plane; D describes an oblique plane. The TRANS root ('across') is the key — it cuts across the long axis of the body, hence horizontal.

questions.stem: The medical term 'VERTIGO' derives from Latin VERTERE (to turn). In clinical usage, which option correctly distinguishes vertigo from acrophobia?

options.option_text: Vertigo is intense fear of heights; acrophobia is a balance disorder
Vertigo is fear of enclosed spaces; acrophobia is fear of open heights
Vertigo is a spinning or whirling sensation; acrophobia is fear of heights
Vertigo is a type of acrophobia that is triggered by circular motion

questions.explanation: C is correct: vertigo is a symptom — a false sensation that the environment or self is spinning (from inner-ear or vestibular dysfunction), etymologically tied to 'turning.' Acrophobia is a phobia — an irrational fear of heights. A is the classic swap error candidates make. B confuses vertigo with claustrophobia. D is wrong because vertigo is not a phobia at all.

questions.stem: The English word 'ANIMADVERSION' is built from ANIMUS (mind) + AD (toward) + VERT (to turn) + ION, meaning literally 'a turning of the mind toward (a fault).' Which sentence uses it with the correct meaning?

options.option_text: Her animadversion on the proposed amendment was full of warm praise
The critic's animadversion on the novel was a stinging rebuke of its style
His animadversion toward trekking made him refuse all outdoor invitations
The animadversion of the old ordinance into a new bill was passed unanimously

questions.explanation: B is correct: 'animadversion' means a sharp critical remark or censure directed at a fault — the mind 'turns toward' the defect to condemn it. A is self-contradictory ('warm praise' inverts the meaning). C is a trap that blends 'animadversion' with 'aversion'; the preposition pattern is also wrong ('aversion toward' works; 'animadversion toward' does not). D misuses it as if it means 'conversion' or 'transformation.'

questions.stem: The word 'CONVERSE' derives from VERS (to turn). In formal logic, the CONVERSE of the statement 'All mammals are warm-blooded animals' is:

options.option_text: No mammals are cold-blooded animals; the negative of the original
Some warm-blooded animals are not mammals; a partial exclusion
All warm-blooded animals are mammals; the claim is turned around
No cold-blooded animals belong to the class of mammals at all

questions.explanation: C is correct: the CONVERSE of 'All A are B' is formed by 'turning around' subject and predicate to get 'All B are A.' Hence 'All warm-blooded animals are mammals' is the converse — and notably, it is FALSE (birds and reptiles can be warm-blooded yet are not mammals). A is the contradiction (negating the predicate). B resembles the obverse. D is an irrelevant statement. The hard insight: a true statement's converse need not be true.
